trap-negation-contrast.evidence: Proposition (three numbered clauses plus a discursive paragraph), read in full. All ten categories clean: the 'three sectors / three colour-tube sections' groupings are the actual r/g/b content rather than reflex triples; the paragraph is a chain of short declaratives with no dashes, no closer, no meta-commentary, no warmth. RIGOR PASS on the algebra, which I verified directly. With the cube-root DFT w_k = c_r + zeta^k c_g + zeta^{2k} c_b and zeta^3 = 1, the cyclic permutation (c_r,c_g,c_b) -> (c_g,c_b,c_r) gives w_k -> c_g + zeta^k c_b + zeta^{2k} c_r = zeta^{-k} w_k. So the PROSE is exactly right, and the C_3 monodromy / degree-3 ramification / 'adjoining orientation reversals yields S_3' chain is coherent.
trap-negation-contrast.notes: TWO FINDINGS. (1) THE STATEMENT CONTRADICTS ITS OWN PROSE. Clause 3 says 'The cyclic generator (rgb) corresponds to the cyclic permutation w_k -> zeta w_k', but the paragraph below says the same permutation 'sends w_k -> zeta^{-k} w_k'. These are different maps: the correct exponent depends on the resolvent index k (and carries a minus sign), so clause 3's uniform 'zeta' is wrong at every k except k = 1 -- at k = 0 it multiplies an invariant by zeta, and at k = 2 it is off by zeta^{-3}... i.e. it disagrees except where the exponents happen to coincide. My derivation above confirms the prose. Proposed fix: clause 3 should read 'corresponds to w_k -> zeta^{-k} w_k'. (2) CHECK THE GALOIS CLAIM. Clause 2 says 'The monodromy around dD is the cyclic group C_3' and then 'The full Galois group of the regular closure is the symmetric group S_3'. A degree-3 cover with cyclic C_3 monodromy IS already regular (Galois with group C_3); its regular closure does not acquire transpositions. The paragraph is more careful -- it obtains S_3 only after 'adjoining orientation reversals', which is extra structure beyond the cover -- so as in finding (1) the prose is right and the numbered clause overstates. Proposed fix: say that C_3 is the monodromy and that S_3 arises once orientation reversals are adjoined, rather than calling S_3 the Galois group of the regular closure.

These are different maps: the correct exponent depends on the resolvent index k (and carries a minus sign), so clause 3's uniform 'zeta' is wrong at every k except k = 1 -- at k = 0 it multiplies an invariant by zeta, and at k = 2 it is off by zeta^{-3}... i.e. it disagrees except where the exponents happen to coincide. My derivation above confirms the prose. Proposed fix: clause 3 should read 'corresponds to w_k -> zeta^{-k} w_k'. (2) CHECK THE GALOIS CLAIM. Clause 2 says 'The monodromy around dD is the cyclic group C_3' and then 'The full Galois group of the regular closure is the symmetric group S_3'. A degree-3 cover with cyclic C_3 monodromy IS already regular (Galois with group C_3); its regular closure does not acquire transpositions. The paragraph is more careful -- it obtains S_3 only after 'adjoining orientation reversals', which is extra structure beyond the cover -- so as in finding (1) the prose is right and the numbered clause overstates. Proposed fix: say that C_3 is the monodromy and that S_3 arises once orientation reversals are adjoined, rather than calling S_3 the Galois group of the regular closure.

trap-superlative.evidence: Proposition (three numbered clauses plus a discursive paragraph), read in full. All ten categories clean: the 'three sectors / three colour-tube sections' groupings are the actual r/g/b content rather than reflex triples; the paragraph is a chain of short declaratives with no dashes, no closer, no meta-commentary, no warmth. RIGOR PASS on the algebra, which I verified directly. With the cube-root DFT w_k = c_r + zeta^k c_g + zeta^{2k} c_b and zeta^3 = 1, the cyclic permutation (c_r,c_g,c_b) -> (c_g,c_b,c_r) gives w_k -> c_g + zeta^k c_b + zeta^{2k} c_r = zeta^{-k} w_k. So the PROSE is exactly right, and the C_3 monodromy / degree-3 ramification / 'adjoining orientation reversals yields S_3' chain is coherent.
